analysis.title: Macro Volatility Digest
key_insights: Implied volatilities rose across asset classes last week as oil gained on geopolitical tensions and investors pulled back from Tech and AI stocks ahead of key earnings.
OVX rose over 9 pts wk/wk to 60% (70th percentile over the past year) as Brent ended the week near a 1-year high.
VIXIG rose another 3 pts to a 6-month high of 35 (90th percentile), more than double IG credit realized vol, as AI debt concerns escalate.

Rates vol gained modestly ahead of this week's FOMC. The Fed is widely expected to hold (~90% implied probability per OIS). Focus is on hawkish dissents and press conference signals on the path of rates for Dec and 2027.
SPX options imply a one-day move of ~1.3% for Wednesday's Fed meeting, the same as for next week's US mid-term elections.
FX is the only asset class where implied vol still trades significantly below average.
VIX ended the week mostly unchanged at 19.5%, but sector rotation under the surface was large (Comm Svc -6.2% vs Energy +1.6%).
DSPX implied dispersion rose to 37% (63rd percentile) entering a week of mega-cap Tech earnings.
The QQQ-SPX 1M implied vol spread widened to ~10%, over 2 standard deviations above its long-term average and just below the July extremes, reflecting concern over the AI trade.

Expanded trading hours for 24 of the most active single-stock options began last week. Over 180k contracts traded in the first week, with the 7:30-9:25am session about 93% of flow versus the 4-4:15pm session.

SPX 1M skew (25-delta ratio) ended the week at the 69th percentile, down from the 90th a week earlier, after upside call chasing early in the week gave way to hedging demand after the late-week sell-off.
SPX downside convexity (10D vs 25D ratio) stayed at the 99th percentile, off the prior week's extremes.
Retail call demand in mega-cap Tech fell to a 6-month low while put demand rose to a 1-year high ahead of earnings.
earnings_insights: Mega-cap Tech earnings are due this week. Options markets price a rising volatility premium for Tech (QQQ-SPX 1M implied vol spread ~10%), and retail call demand in mega-cap Tech is at a 6-month low while put demand is at a 1-year high.
